The Incomparable Roberta Flack 🎤✨ #RobertaFlack #SoulMusic #Shorts

short // Apr 8, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

Some voices don't need to be loud to stop a room. Roberta Flack's was one of them.

In this short, I put together a few timeless moments from the legendary Roberta Flack: "Killing Me Softly with His Song," "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" and "Tonight, I Celebrate My Love." One minute isn't close to enough, but it's a start.

The voice

Roberta Flack could make a song feel like a private conversation. She didn't oversing. She slowed things down, held back and let every word land, and somehow that hit harder than any big note.

She was a trained musician, too. She started out as a classical piano prodigy, earned a music scholarship to Howard University at 15, and taught music before her career took off. You can hear that control in everything she recorded.

Back-to-back Record of the Year

Here's a stat that still sounds made up: Roberta Flack was the first artist to win the Grammy for Record of the Year two years in a row.

  • "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" won in 1973. The song got a second life after Clint Eastwood used it in Play Misty for Me.
  • "Killing Me Softly with His Song" won in 1974.

The songs in this tribute

"Killing Me Softly with His Song" is the one everybody knows, and a whole new generation found it through the Fugees' 1996 cover. But her version is the blueprint.

"The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" is almost five minutes of patience. It's slow, spare and completely hypnotic.

"Tonight, I Celebrate My Love," her 1983 duet with Peabo Bryson, is a quiet storm classic that has played at weddings and anniversaries for decades.

And that's before you get to "Feel Like Makin' Love," or her duets with Donny Hathaway, like "Where Is the Love" and "The Closer I Get to You."

Why she matters

Roberta Flack proved that soul music could be soft and still be powerful. A lot of the R&B that came after her, from quiet storm radio to neo-soul, owes something to the space she made.

She died in February 2025, at 88, after living with ALS. Her songs are going to outlive all of us.

Quick answers

What are Roberta Flack's most famous songs? "Killing Me Softly with His Song," "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face," "Feel Like Makin' Love," "Where Is the Love" and "The Closer I Get to You" with Donny Hathaway, and "Tonight, I Celebrate My Love" with Peabo Bryson.

Did Roberta Flack win Record of the Year twice? Yes. She was the first artist to win it two years in a row, for "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" in 1973 and "Killing Me Softly with His Song" in 1974.

Who sang "Killing Me Softly" first? Lori Lieberman recorded it first, in 1972, but Roberta Flack's 1973 version made it a classic.

When did Roberta Flack die? On February 24, 2025, at age 88.
